texts.preamble: Md Ajmal Baig vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 12 June, 2023 Author: K. Lakshman Bench: K.Lakshman, P.Sree Sudha Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman And Hon'Ble Smt Justice P. Sree Sudha Writ Petition No.44557 of 2022 Order:
texts.facts: 3. Perusal of the record would reveal that two criminal cases were registered against the detenu i.e., Crime No.799 of 2021 pending on the file of Raidurgam Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 21(a),(c), 22 and 29 of N.D.P.S. Act and Crime No.615 of 2022 pending on the file of RC Puram Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 8 r/w.21(b) of N.D.P.S. Act. In the first Crime 183 Grams of Cocaine and 44 MDMA Ecstasy pills, weighing 22 grams were seized. He was released on bail on 07-06-2022. 4. Second crime was registered on 25-08-2022 and 30 Grams of Cocaine was seized from the detenu. He was released on bail on 15-11-2022 itself. Impugned detention order was passed on 25-11-2022 i.e., ten (10) days after the detenu obtaining bail in the 2nd crime. 5. It is relevant to note that as per Section 37(1)(B)(2) of NDPS Act, 1985 the Court while granting bail has to satisfy itself that there are reasonable grounds for believing that accused is not guilty of such offence for and that he is not likely to commit any offence while on bail. Considering the said aspects, Court below granted bail to the petitioner in the first crime. Even then, respondent authorities have not filed any application seeking cancellation of bail granted to the detenu in the first crime on the ground that he has involved in the similar offence. 6. It is relevant to note that in the detention order, respondent No.2 stated that to prevent detenu from committing the similar offences, he has invoked the provisions of The Telangana Prevention Of Md Ajmal Baig vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6522232/ 1 Dangerous Activities Of Boot-Leggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders Land- Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders And White Collar Or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (for short, 'the Act, 1986') by issuing detention order. But the Investing Officer failed to file an application seeking cancellation of bail granted to the detenu in the first crime i.e., Cr.No.799 of 2021 on ground that detenu has involved in the second crime Cr.No.615 of 2022 dated 25.08.2022 for the similar offences. Without availing said alternative remedies i.e., opposing the bail application in second crime and filing application seeking cancellation of bail in the first crime, respondent No.2 has passed detention order dated 25.11.2022.
texts.arguments: 7. In Ram Manohar Lohia vs. State of Bihar1 Hon'ble Apex Court held as under: "Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some ? The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them. Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder. Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder. When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder, Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions. (1966) 1 SCR 709 It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State." Md Ajmal Baig vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6522232/ 2 8. In Banka Sneha Sheela v. State of Telangana2 Hon'ble Apex Court held that mere apprehension of breach of law (2021) 9 SCC 415 and order cannot be a ground to invoke the harsh provisions of preventive detention. The authorities have a remedy to oppose the bail application or file for cancellation of bail, if they feel that release of such persons is against the interest of society. 13. In Harikisan V/s State of Maharashtra and others3 and Hadibandhu Das Vs/ District Magistrate, Cuttack and another4 constitutional bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court categorically held that service of entire material in vernacular language within the mandatory period is must. Section 8 of the Act, 1986 read as follows: "8. Grounds of order of detention to be disclosed to persons affected by the order: Md Ajmal Baig vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6522232/ 3 (1) When a person is detained in pursuance of a detention order, the authority making the order shall as soon as may be but not later than five days from the date of detention, communicate to him the grounds on which the order has been made and shall afford him the 1962 Supp(2) SCR 918 : AIR 1962 SC 911: (1962) 1 Cri LJ797 (1969) 1SCR 227 : AIR 1969 SC 43 : 1969 Cri LJ 274 earliest opportunity of making a representation against the order to the Government. (2) Nothing in sub-section (1) shall require the authority to disclose facts which it considers to be against the public interest to disclose."
